History of Astronomy: Geocentric model
The ancient view placing Earth at the centre of the universe
Heliocentric model
The view placing the Sun at the centre of the solar system
Ptolemy
The astronomer whose epicycle model dominated for over a thousand years
Epicycle
A small circle added to an orbit to explain retrograde motion
Copernicus
The astronomer who revived the heliocentric model in 1543
Tycho Brahe
The observer who recorded planetary positions with unmatched precision
Johannes Kepler
The astronomer who derived elliptical orbits from Brahe's data
Galileo Galilei
The first to use a telescope systematically, finding Jupiter's moons
Phases of Venus
Galileo's observation that disproved the pure geocentric model
Isaac Newton
The scientist who explained orbits with universal gravitation
Law of universal gravitation
Attraction proportional to masses and inversely to distance squared
Edwin Hubble
The astronomer who showed galaxies exist beyond the Milky Way and recede
Parallax
The apparent shift of a nearby star against distant background stars
Celestial sphere
The imaginary sphere on which sky objects appear to sit

The Earth-Moon System: Rotation
The spin of a body on its own axis
Revolution
The orbit of one body around another
Axial tilt
Earth's 23.5 degree tilt, the cause of the seasons
Solstice
The day of maximum or minimum daylight in a hemisphere
Equinox
A day of nearly equal daylight and darkness worldwide
Synchronous rotation
The Moon rotating once per orbit, keeping one face toward Earth
Near side and far side
The permanently visible hemisphere versus the hidden one
Lunar phases
The changing illuminated fraction seen from Earth
Waxing versus waning
The lit portion growing versus shrinking
Synodic month
The 29.5-day cycle from new moon to new moon
Solar eclipse
The Moon passing between Earth and the Sun
Lunar eclipse
Earth's shadow falling across the Moon
Umbra and penumbra
The full shadow versus the partial shadow
Tides
The rise and fall of sea level from lunar and solar gravity
Spring and neap tides
Maximum tidal range at syzygy versus minimum at quadrature
Giant impact hypothesis
The theory that the Moon formed from debris of a collision
The Solar System: The Sun and everything gravitationally bound to it
Formation from a collapsing, rotating cloud of gas and dust
Small particles sticking together to build planetesimals
The distance beyond which volatiles could condense into ice
Orbits are ellipses with the Sun at one focus
A planet sweeps equal areas in equal times

The closest and farthest points of an orbit from the Sun

The icy region beyond Neptune containing Pluto
The distant spherical shell believed to source long-period comets
A round body that has not cleared its orbital neighbourhood
Terrestrial and Gas Planets: A small, dense, rocky planet with a solid surface
A large, low-density gas or ice giant
The smallest planet, closest to the Sun, with extreme temperature swings
A planet with a runaway greenhouse effect and crushing surface pressure
The red planet, with the largest volcano and evidence of ancient water

The planet best known for its extensive ring system
A disc of ice and rock particles orbiting a planet
An ice giant rotating on its side, tilted about 98 degrees

Saturn's largest moon, with a thick atmosphere and liquid methane lakes

Carbon dioxide trapping heat, giving surface temperatures near 460 Celsius
Comets, Asteroids, and Meteors: Asteroid
A rocky body orbiting the Sun, mostly between Mars and Jupiter
Asteroid belt
The region of rocky debris between Mars and Jupiter
Ceres
The largest asteroid belt object, classified as a dwarf planet
Comet
An icy body that develops a coma and tail near the Sun
Nucleus of a comet
The solid icy core, often described as a dirty snowball
Coma
The glowing cloud of gas and dust surrounding a comet's nucleus
Ion tail
A comet tail of charged gas pointing directly away from the Sun
Dust tail
A curved comet tail of particles trailing along the orbit
Short-period comet
A comet returning in under two hundred years, from the Kuiper Belt
Meteoroid
A small rocky fragment travelling through space
Meteor
The streak of light produced as a meteoroid burns in the atmosphere
Meteorite
A fragment that survives and reaches the ground
Meteor shower
Many meteors seen as Earth crosses a comet's debris trail
Near-Earth object
An asteroid or comet whose orbit brings it close to Earth
Impact crater
A bowl-shaped depression formed by a high-speed collision
The Sun: The Sun
A main-sequence star of spectral type G powering the solar system
Core of the Sun
The central region where hydrogen fuses into helium
Nuclear fusion
Light nuclei combining to release enormous energy
Proton-proton chain
The fusion sequence that powers Sun-like stars
Radiative zone
The layer where energy moves outward as photons
Convective zone
The layer where hot gas physically rises and cool gas sinks
Photosphere
The visible surface of the Sun
Chromosphere
The reddish layer above the photosphere
Corona
The Sun's outer atmosphere, far hotter than the surface
Sunspot
A cooler, darker region of intense magnetic activity
Solar cycle
The roughly eleven-year rise and fall in sunspot activity
Solar flare
A sudden intense burst of radiation from the Sun
Coronal mass ejection
A large expulsion of plasma and magnetic field
Solar wind
The continuous stream of charged particles leaving the Sun
Aurora
Glowing light from solar particles striking the upper atmosphere
Stellar Classification and Evolution: Luminosity
The total energy a star radiates per second
Apparent magnitude
How bright a star appears from Earth
Absolute magnitude
How bright a star would be at a standard distance
Spectral class
The OBAFGKM sequence ordering stars from hottest to coolest
Hertzsprung-Russell diagram
A plot of luminosity against surface temperature
Main sequence
The band of stars fusing hydrogen in their cores
Stellar nursery
A nebula where gravity collapses gas into new stars
Protostar
A contracting cloud not yet hot enough for fusion
Red giant
A swollen, cool late stage of a low- or medium-mass star
Planetary nebula
The expanding shell of gas shed by a dying Sun-like star
White dwarf
The dense Earth-sized remnant of a low-mass star
Supergiant
An enormous late stage of a massive star
Supernova
The catastrophic explosion ending a massive star's life
Mass and stellar lifetime
More massive stars burn hotter and die far sooner
Nucleosynthesis
The creation of heavier elements inside stars
Binary star system
Two stars orbiting a common centre of mass
Black Holes and Neutron Stars: Neutron star
An extremely dense remnant composed almost entirely of neutrons
Pulsar
A rapidly rotating neutron star emitting beamed radiation
Chandrasekhar limit
The 1.4 solar mass ceiling above which a white dwarf collapses
Black hole
An object whose gravity prevents even light from escaping
Event horizon
The boundary beyond which nothing can return
Schwarzschild radius
The radius of the event horizon for a given mass
Singularity
The theoretical point of infinite density at a black hole's centre
Stellar-mass black hole
A black hole formed from the collapse of a massive star
Supermassive black hole
A black hole of millions to billions of solar masses in a galaxy core
Accretion disk
Superheated matter spiralling into a compact object
Gravitational lensing
Massive objects bending light from behind them
Time dilation near a black hole
Clocks running slower in strong gravity
Hawking radiation
Theoretical particle emission causing black holes to slowly evaporate
Gravitational waves
Ripples in spacetime detected from merging compact objects
Galaxies: A gravitationally bound system of stars, gas, dust, and dark matter
A galaxy with a central bulge and winding arms of young stars
A spiral with a straight bar of stars crossing its centre
A rounded galaxy of mostly old stars with little gas
A galaxy without a symmetric structure, often from interaction
The spherical region of old stars and globular clusters around a galaxy
A dense spherical group of hundreds of thousands of old stars
A loose group of young stars formed together in the disc
Unseen mass inferred from galactic rotation and lensing
Flat outer velocities that revealed dark matter
An extremely bright core powered by a supermassive black hole
An extremely luminous distant active galactic nucleus
The galaxy cluster containing the Milky Way and Andromeda
A merger that reshapes galaxies and triggers star formation

The model that the universe expanded from a hot dense state
Light stretched to longer wavelengths as a source recedes
The measured present-day rate of cosmic expansion
Leftover radiation from when the universe became transparent
Space itself stretching rather than galaxies flying through it
The distance light travels in one year
Seeing distant objects as they were when the light left them
The region whose light has had time to reach us
The unexplained influence accelerating cosmic expansion
A brief period of extremely rapid early expansion
The formation of hydrogen and helium in the first minutes
The Search for Life: Astrobiology
The study of the possibility and nature of life beyond Earth
Habitable zone
The orbital range where liquid water can exist on a surface
Exoplanet
A planet orbiting a star other than the Sun
Transit method
Detecting a planet by the dip in starlight as it crosses
Radial velocity method
Detecting a planet by the wobble it induces in its star
Direct imaging
Photographing an exoplanet by blocking its star's light
Biosignature
A chemical or spectral clue suggesting biological activity
Extremophile
An organism thriving in conditions once thought lethal
Subsurface ocean
Liquid water beneath an icy crust, as on Europa and Enceladus
Drake equation
A framework estimating the number of communicating civilisations
Fermi paradox
The tension between high probability estimates and no observed contact
SETI
The organised search for extraterrestrial intelligence via radio signals
Panspermia
The hypothesis that life or its precursors travel between worlds
Goldilocks conditions
The combination of factors that make a world suitable for life
